newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - No move seen in Bank of Spain rate Monday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - No move seen in Bank of Spain rate Monday.

text.p: The Spanish central bank will hold its key money market rate unchanged at 5.25 percent on Monday, though it is likely to use its scope to cut as soon as uncertainty over the European economic and monetary union (EMU) is resolved, a poll showed on Friday.

According to 12 out of 13 economists polled after the release of a Spanish May Consumer Price Index --which came out as expected at 1.5 percent year-on-year down from 1.7 percent in April-- Monday's official repurchase auction would see the key rate held stable.
The possibility of EMU jitters after the Amsterdam summit and a widespread forecast that Spanish inflation will bottom at this level are the main reasons behind this prediction.

"If the core rate had been slightly better than expected, we'd go for a cut in the key rate on Monday. But as this wasn't the case, the other factor will weigh, that's the euro and the markets, and prudence by the Bank of Spain will be useful so it can keep a margin until the next (repo) auction." said Yolanda Fernandez, analyst at Analistas Financieros Internacionales in Madrid.
But as EMU tensions were likely to fade away, seven out of 13 economists were expecting the Bank of Spain could sanction its fifth rate cut this year on June 24, at the following repo operation.
"I think the Bank of Spain will wait for the Amsterdam summit and for the solution of the budget stability pact," said Carmen Hernansanz, economist at Merrill Lynch in Madrid.

The Bank of Spain last cut its key money market rate on May 16 by 25 basis points to 5.25 percent. It started the current downtrend in official rates in December 1995 when it cut its repo rate from 9.25 percent.
